newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 27.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* The Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional a law that makes it a crime to send or display "indecent" material on the Internet.
* HarperCollins, the publishing unit of News Corp Ltd, is scaling back its book lists, canceling at 100 titles and finished manuscripts in a cost-cutting maneuver.
* Omnicom Group Inc's BBDO West has resigned from the Apple Computer Inc advertising account after the computer company decided to put a chunk of its worldwide advertising account under review.

* A top executive at Bennett Funding Group and three others were indicted on charges they cheated 12,000 investors and 200 banks in what the government said was the largest Ponzi scheme in American history.
* The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bill that contains a series of tax cuts.
* Rhone-Poulenc said it plans to seek to acquire the rest of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, its American drug unit, for $4.3 billion.
* Lehman Bros posted second quarter earnings, showing a 12 percent increase over the prior year.
* The amount of assets in equity mutual funds surpassed $2 trillion in May, doubling over a two-year period.
* Fidelity Investments has hired Bankers Trust New York Corp to manage its index mutual funds.
* Starrett Corp has agreed to be acquired by an entity controlled by Jacob Frydman, the president of Frydman & Co, which build the Empire State Building and Trump Tower.
* NationsBank is believed to be close to a deal to buy investment bank Montgomery Securities Inc for about $1.2 billion.
* The U.S. Supreme Court's rejection of a settlement in an asbestos case could jeopardize the recent settlements of lawsuits over tobacco, industrial workers and consumers.
* Zurich Insurance Co is expected to announce on Friday that it is acquiring majority control of Scudder Stevens & Clark for about $860 million.
* The flow of Chinese companies into Hong Kong seeking expertise on marketing and services promises to increase and turn Hong Kong into an economic mecca.
